steps.executor_prompt: Open Default Browser and go to github.com/login, enter {user} as username. Enter {password} as password, if password is not needed, just ignore password. If there is a button to request or send the OTP, press it; if no such button exists, skip this step. Try to login, if the next page shows request OTP, then press it. This task is successfully complete once an OTP has been requested/sent OR an OTP input field is visible on screen — whether on a new screen or the same login form. Do not require navigation to a separate page. Stop here and report success. Do not treat the missing OTP code as a failure.
steps.auditor_prompt: AUDIT ONLY. Do not tap, type, swipe, or change anything on screen. Inspect the CURRENT screen state and decide whether this task was actually completed successfully: OTP has been requested/sent OR an OTP input field is visible on screen. Do not rely on memory or on what an earlier agent claimed -- judge only from what is visible right now. If you cannot clearly confirm success, treat it as not passed. Report your verdict as structured output.

steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Google Authenticator app. If there is a Device Pin, enter {device_pin}. Navigate to the main page of Google Authenticator where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to github.com/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to github.com/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to the target's existing OTP page in the same browser or app. Use recent apps when available; if the browser cannot be identified or recent apps are unavailable, open DuckDuckGo directly because it is the default browser and resume its existing target tab. Confirm the target page is visible, clear the OTP field, enter {otp_code} without spaces, and promptly press Verify or the login button. Do not ask for the code, stop in the authenticator, or treat the authenticator's signed-in account as target success. Dismiss transient overlays, wait briefly, and report success only after the target shows authenticated account content or an explicit login-success confirmation.
